title: When a Drug Becomes a Test

scenes.tts: Chapter one linked free subunits, ends, and their lattice. How can a drug turn that rule into a clean test?
scenes.visual: Reuse chapter 1's COLOR MAP: fresh-nucleotide subunits GOLD, old ADP or GDP subunits BLUE, tight end GREEN, loose end RED, free-subunit gauge TEAL, text TEXT. Add drug perturbations in MAGENTA throughout. From the first frame, carry over chapter 1's world: a large actin filament across the upper half and a microtubule across the lower half, both labelled 'schematic'. Gold free subunits drift at left, both polymers' active ends move at centre, and blue lattice extends right. Three faint MAGENTA question marks travel in sequence from the free pool to an end to the lattice. On the question, a single MAGENTA drug chip enters from above, splits into three ghost positions over those sites, and leaves the polymers moving underneath.
scenes.narration: Chapter one linked free subunits, ends, and their lattice. How can a drug turn that rule into a clean test?

scenes.visual: Title card (TitleCard): LESSON 'Cytoskeletal Polymers and Dynamics', TITLE 'When a Drug Becomes a Test'. Gold subunits continue drifting and the filament ends keep moving behind the title.

scenes.tts: A drug is informative only when three labels stay attached: its target, dose, and test system. Remove any label, and the same drug name can support the wrong conclusion.
scenes.visual: Return to the same two polymers. The MAGENTA drug chip docks in the centre of a large TEXT sentence card built from three connected tags: 'target' beside a simple site marker, 'dose' beside a rising gauge, and 'system' beside a dish outline. On 'stay attached', the tags lock to the drug chip with short bright links. On 'Remove any label', first the site marker, then gauge, then dish briefly detach; each time the conclusion arrow below swings between two different outcomes. All three reconnect before the scene ends.
scenes.narration: A drug is informative only when three labels stay attached: its target, dose, and test system. Remove any label, and the same drug name can support the wrong conclusion.

scenes.tts: Keep the moving parts on screen. Free subunits feed an end; the end adds to or removes from a lattice. A perturbation can act at any of those three places.
scenes.visual: Use the actin filament as one continuous assembly line filling most of the frame. TEAL free-pool gauge at left feeds drifting GOLD actin blocks toward the GREEN barbed end in the middle; older BLUE filament continues to the right. On 'Free subunits', one outlined subunit travels from pool to end and joins. On 'removes', one old block leaves the far end. On 'three places', a MAGENTA spotlight slides along this same path and pauses over three large labels in sequence: 'free pool', 'end', 'lattice'. Mark the whole diagram 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Keep the moving parts on screen. Free subunits feed an end; the end adds to or removes from a lattice. A perturbation can act at any of those three places.

scenes.tts: Latrunculin A binds actin monomers one to one, holding them so they cannot join. The available pool falls, so less actin enters polymer. Yet it can also speed loss at the ends of freshly built filaments. Sequestration is not the whole story.
scenes.visual: Stay on the actin assembly line. On 'binds actin monomers', MAGENTA cups labelled 'latrunculin A' close around individual GOLD free subunits, one cup per subunit; a small 'one to one' counter increments in pairs. Cupped subunits drift but cannot enter the end. On 'pool falls', the TEAL available-subunit gauge drops and end growth slows. On 'also speed loss', a newly built stretch of GOLD (fresh) blocks at each end, labelled 'fresh filament', gets a second small MAGENTA arrow and those GOLD blocks leave faster from both ends; older BLUE stretches keep their pace (the effect was seen only on freshly assembled ATP-actin filaments). A large bracket first labelled 'sequestration' expands to include both the pool and end arrows, then changes to 'more than sequestration'.
scenes.narration: Latrunculin A binds actin monomers one to one, holding them so they cannot join. The available pool falls, so less actin enters polymer. Yet it can also speed loss at the ends of freshly built filaments. Sequestration is not the whole story.

scenes.tts: Cytochalasin B acts elsewhere. Its binding follows filament-end number, not total actin, and it inhibits addition at barbed ends. Phalloidin instead binds along actin filaments. With purified muscle actin, it slows disassembly.
scenes.visual: Clear the latrunculin cups while keeping the same schematic filament. On 'Cytochalasin B', one actin-coated bead transforms into several beads carrying shorter filaments; their combined BLUE actin length stays fixed while the number of ends rises. MAGENTA chips labelled 'cytochalasin B' gather at GREEN barbed ends. A counter 'ends' rises while 'total actin' stays level, and a drug-binding gauge follows the end count. Gold blocks bounce away from the occupied barbed ends. On 'Phalloidin instead', reset to one filament and transform the end-bound chips into MAGENTA side clips along the BLUE lattice, labelled 'phalloidin'. At the pointed end, the loss counter slows. Add a visible dish label 'purified muscle actin'.
scenes.narration: Cytochalasin B acts elsewhere. Its binding follows filament-end number, not total actin, and it inhibits addition at barbed ends. Phalloidin instead binds along actin filaments. With purified muscle actin, it slows disassembly.

scenes.tts: Now predict. A drug lowers the amount of polymer. Does that observation alone reveal whether it trapped subunits, blocked ends, or changed the lattice?
scenes.visual: Transform the moving actin world into one large balance display labelled 'polymer amount, schematic'. Its bar falls from high to low. Beneath it, show three equally sized MAGENTA question-mark doors positioned along the carried pathway: a free GOLD subunit entering door one, a filament end entering door two, and a BLUE lattice segment entering door three. The question fills the upper third in TEXT. Each door pulses once, but no answer appears.
scenes.narration: Now predict. A drug lowers the amount of polymer. Does that observation alone reveal whether it trapped subunits, blocked ends, or changed the lattice?

scenes.visual: Hold the same prediction question and low polymer bar for 4.5 seconds. The three MAGENTA doors breathe gently and gold free subunits drift, but none opens and no answer is revealed.

scenes.tts: No. The same amount change can begin at different sites. Add a second measurement that separates them. Holding total actin constant while changing end number can reveal binding that follows ends.
scenes.visual: On 'No', the three doors open onto three different mechanisms, each leading to the same low polymer bar, so the bar alone cannot distinguish them. On 'second measurement', keep the end-binding path and replace the amount bar with two plots side by side, both labelled 'schematic'. Plot one: drug binding (y) against end number (x), rising. Plot two: total actin (y) for the same samples (x), a flat line. Animate one actin-coated bead becoming several beads with more filament ends but the same combined filament length; the plotted end count and MAGENTA binding signal rise together.
scenes.narration: No. The same amount change can begin at different sites. Add a second measurement that separates them. Holding total actin constant while changing end number can reveal binding that follows ends.

scenes.tts: That is the difference between an effect and a mechanism. Polymer amount reports the outcome. A measurement tied to the proposed target tests how that outcome arose.
scenes.visual: Keep the schematic end-number plot large. On 'effect', the single low polymer bar moves to a box labelled 'effect: less polymer'. On 'mechanism', the changing end count and the rising drug-binding points move into a second box labelled 'mechanism test'. Draw an arrow from changed end number through changed binding to the effect box, with each step animated from the counted filaments. On 'proposed target', the MAGENTA end marker from scene five locks onto the plot's rising points while the free-pool and lattice doors fade back as alternatives not tested by this measurement.
scenes.narration: That is the difference between an effect and a mechanism. Polymer amount reports the outcome. A measurement tied to the proposed target tests how that outcome arose.

scenes.tts: Target is still not enough; dose changes the experiment. In tested cultured cells, nanomolar nocodazole can pause microtubules and slow growth and shortening. Micromolar doses commonly used on cultured mammalian cells remove most microtubules.
scenes.visual: Transform the actin filament and plots into the carried microtubule world from chapter 1: a BLUE tube with a GOLD cap grows and shortens above a MAGENTA dose gauge. Mark the view 'schematic'. On 'nanomolar', keep the gauge low; the end spends time paused and both its upward growth and downward shortening arrows become shorter. On 'Micromolar', raise the gauge by three labelled steps to 'micromolar'; the tube shortens back toward the cell centre and most radial microtubules in a simple cultured-cell outline disappear. Keep two separate outcome labels attached to their dose levels.
scenes.narration: Target is still not enough; dose changes the experiment. In tested cultured cells, nanomolar nocodazole can pause microtubules and slow growth and shortening. Micromolar doses commonly used on cultured mammalian cells remove most microtubules.

scenes.tts: The system can change a switching result too. With nocodazole, catastrophe became more frequent in cultured newt lung cells. In B S C one monkey kidney cells after an hour, catastrophe became less frequent.
scenes.caption: The system can change a switching result too. With nocodazole, catastrophe became more frequent in cultured newt lung cells. In BSC-1 monkey kidney cells after an hour, catastrophe became less frequent.
scenes.visual: Split one culture dish into two large dishes, each with its own MAGENTA nocodazole chip; label no dose and do not imply the two doses were matched (the BSC-1 dose is not stated in the abstract). Left label: 'newt lung cells'; right label: 'BSC-1 cells, 1 hour'. Inside each, identical microtubules grow, with one visible 'schematic' label spanning the comparison. A RED catastrophe counter above the left dish speeds up, while the matching counter above the right dish slows down. A central arrow from the unchanged nocodazole chip branches to opposite arrows labelled 'more catastrophes' and 'fewer catastrophes'. Do not imply that every nocodazole effect reverses; highlight only the catastrophe counter.
scenes.narration: The system can change a switching result too. With nocodazole, catastrophe became more frequent in cultured newt lung cells. In BSC-1 monkey kidney cells after an hour, catastrophe became less frequent.

scenes.tts: Phalloidin shows another system boundary. It slows disassembly with purified muscle actin, but enters living cells poorly. Fluorescent phalloidin therefore mainly stains filaments after cells are fixed.
scenes.visual: Transform the two dishes into a large side-by-side comparison using the same actin filament; keep a visible 'schematic' label on the comparison. Left is an open dish labelled 'purified muscle actin'; MAGENTA phalloidin side clips reach the filament and its BLUE blocks stop leaving. Right is a cell outline labelled 'living cell'; identical clips collect outside its membrane while the internal filament continues moving. On 'after cells are fixed', replace that view with a pale cell and a large label 'fixed-cell stain'; fluorescent MAGENTA clips appear along the filament without animating an entry mechanism. Keep the system label attached to every outcome.
scenes.narration: Phalloidin shows another system boundary. It slows disassembly with purified muscle actin, but enters living cells poorly. Fluorescent phalloidin therefore mainly stains filaments after cells are fixed.

scenes.tts: Sometimes the drug is not selective enough. Withaferin A redistributes vimentin in human fibroblasts, but did not alter purified vimentin assembly. Removing vimentin genetically, then adding it back, is the cleaner test.
scenes.visual: Transform the actin filament into a thick GREY rope labelled 'vimentin' inside a large fibroblast outline, marked 'schematic'. On 'Withaferin A', a MAGENTA chip enters and the rope gathers beside a simple nucleus circle. Alongside it, other unlabeled filament lines also shift, and a warning tag 'not selective' appears. On 'did not alter', move the same rope into a purified-protein dish; it assembles at the same schematic rate with and without the chip. On 'Removing vimentin genetically', return to two matched cells: the left lacks the GREY rope, then the right gains it back from a labelled 'vimentin add-back' block. A GREEN check appears over this paired comparison.
scenes.narration: Sometimes the drug is not selective enough. Withaferin A redistributes vimentin in human fibroblasts, but did not alter purified vimentin assembly. Removing vimentin genetically, then adding it back, is the cleaner test.

scenes.tts: Read every result as a complete sentence: this target, at this dose, in this system, changed this measurement. Then compare another perturbation aimed at a different step.
scenes.visual: Bring back the connected tags from scene two around one central result card. Build the sentence left to right as moving objects settle into slots: a site marker into 'this target', the MAGENTA gauge into 'at this dose', a dish into 'in this system', and the changing end counter into 'changed this measurement'. On 'compare another perturbation', duplicate the result card below, swap only the site marker for a genetic add-back block, and align the two conclusion arrows. Keep both cards large and inside the safe frame.
scenes.narration: Read every result as a complete sentence: this target, at this dose, in this system, changed this measurement. Then compare another perturbation aimed at a different step.

scenes.tts: Chapter one supplied the moving parts behind cytoskeletal turnover. This chapter adds the rule for testing them experimentally. If target, dose, or system changes, the conclusion may change too.
scenes.visual: The result cards transform back into chapter 1's full moving world: TEAL free pool, GREEN and RED ends, GOLD cap, and BLUE lattices, still visibly labelled 'schematic'. The MAGENTA drug chip travels to one site while its target, dose, and system tags remain tethered above it. On 'rule for testing', the three tags lock into a single frame around the observed motion. On 'may change too', briefly change only the dose, then only the dish, and show the outcome arrow adjust each time without claiming a particular new outcome. End with the three tags bright and the polymers still moving.
scenes.narration: Chapter one supplied the moving parts behind cytoskeletal turnover. This chapter adds the rule for testing them experimentally. If target, dose, or system changes, the conclusion may change too.

scenes.visual: End card (EndCard), LINE: 'A drug tests mechanism only with target, dose, and system.' The three connected tags remain visible behind Hex while filament ends move faintly.
